journey.title: Tab away after typing an unavailable delivery date
journey.goal: Leaving the date field with Tab closes the calendar even when the typed date is outside the delivery window

steps.title: Type a date outside the delivery window

functionalJourney.title: Move the delivery into June with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking through the calendar to June and choosing a day fills the delivery date

guards.title: Type a valid delivery date and Tab away
guards.goal: A correctly typed date is committed and the calendar closes when the user tabs away

plan.root_cause: The datepicker remains open when the input loses focus via Tab if the entered date is outside the allowed min/max range, because the blur/update logic does not trigger hide for invalid dates.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field that explicitly hides the picker, ensuring the calendar closes on focus loss regardless of date validity.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate away from the date field without trapping focus in the datepicker popup, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 2.4.3 Focus Order.
functional_risks: May hide the picker when user intends to correct the date after blur, but blur only occurs when focus has left the field.
Could interfere with custom logic that relies on blur for validation, though existing update() logic remains unchanged.
verification_requirements: Typing a valid date and pressing Tab closes the datepicker.
Typing an invalid date (outside min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker.
Clicking outside the picker still closes it.
Selecting a date from the picker grid works as before.
Inline datepickers are unaffected by the change.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker remains open when the input loses focus via Tab if the entered date is outside the allowed min/max range, because the blur/update logic does not trigger hide for invalid dates. The previous fix added a blur listener but called `this.hide()` on the datepicker instance, which does not have a hide method; the picker instance (`this.picker`) does.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field that explicitly calls `picker.hide()` (the Picker instance) to ensure the calendar closes on focus loss regardless of date validity.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate away from the date field without trapping focus in the datepicker popup, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 2.4.3 Focus Order.
functional_risks: May hide the picker when user intends to correct the date after blur, but blur only occurs when focus has left the field.
Could interfere with custom logic that relies on blur for validation, though existing update() logic remains unchanged.
verification_requirements: Typing a valid date and pressing Tab closes the datepicker.
Typing an invalid date (outside min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker.
Clicking outside the picker still closes it.
Selecting a date from the picker grid works as before.
Inline datepickers are unaffected by the change.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker remains open when the input loses focus via Tab if the entered date is outside the allowed min/max range, because the blur/update logic does not trigger hide for invalid dates. The non-inline picker's event listeners lack a blur handler on the input field to close the picker when focus leaves.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field in the non-inline picker setup that calls `picker.hide()` (the Picker instance) to ensure the calendar closes on focus loss regardless of date validity.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate away from the date field without trapping focus in the datepicker popup, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 2.4.3 Focus Order.
functional_risks: May hide the picker when user intends to correct the date after blur, but blur only occurs when focus has left the field.
Could interfere with custom logic that relies on blur for validation, though existing update() logic remains unchanged.

Typing an invalid date (outside min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker.
Clicking outside the picker still closes it.
Selecting a date from the picker grid works as before.
Inline datepickers are unaffected by the change.
